object_description: compact deep block with a plinth and three continuous atriums
design_condition: the compact volume sits in the south-western area of the site, with a storey-high offset separating an upper entrance terrace and playground from the lower sports fields

positive: A square is created between the new volume and the existing hall
Wildflower meadows and loosely scattered trees line the new building
Public uses such as school management, media library and assembly hall are positively placed on the ground floor
The plinth floor is lit from two sides and the gymnasiums are naturally lit through the level offset
Placing the main entrance at the north-east corner is a clever solution
Entrance, foyer and assembly hall have a pleasant and generous overheight
The open main staircase vertically connects all floors
The escape route problem can be solved with two closed staircases on the east and west facades
Three continuous atriums naturally light the deep interior and offer views and space
negative: The storey-high offset divides the site unconvincingly in the gently sloping terrain
The lower level has its own scale and structure unrelated to the upper level
No dialogue is possible between the central zone and the outdoor space
Light intensity in the atriums seems rather low on the lower floors
Overlapping structural concepts lead to spatial constraints
The ostensible flexibility is only partially given
Access zones become corridors lacking spatial quality when used as learning landscapes
The strong basic concept of the first stage has been obscured in essential parts
